title: Federated Learning for MRI-based BrainAGE: a multicenter study on post-stroke functional outcome prediction
abstract: arXiv:2506.15626v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: $\textbf{Objective:}$ Brain-predicted age difference (BrainAGE) is a neuroimaging biomarker reflecting brain health. However, training robust BrainAGE models requires large datasets, often restricted by privacy concerns. This study evaluates the performance of federated learning (FL) for BrainAGE estimation in ischemic stroke patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy, and investigates its association with clinical phenotypes and functional outcomes.   $\textbf{Methods:}$ We used FLAIR brain images from 1674 stroke patients across 16 hospital centers. We implemented standard machine learning and deep learning models for BrainAGE estimates under three data management strategies: centralized learning (pooled data), FL (local training at each site), and single-site learning. translated_title: 基于MRI脑龄差（BrainAGE）的联邦学习：一项关于卒中后功能结局预测的多中心研究
translated_abstract: 目的：脑预测年龄差（BrainAGE）是一种反映大脑健康的神经影像学生物标志物。然而，训练稳健的BrainAGE模型需要大型数据集，而这往往受到隐私问题的限制。本研究评估了联邦学习（FL）在接受机械取栓治疗的缺血性卒中患者中进行BrainAGE估计的性能，并探讨其与临床表型和功能结局之间的关联。方法：我们使用了来自16家医院中心共1674名卒中患者的FLAIR脑部影像数据。我们在三种数据管理策略下实现了用于BrainAGE估计的标准机器学习和深度学习模型：集中式学习（汇总数据）、联邦学习（各站点本地训练）以及单站点学习。我们报告了预测误差，并检验了BrainAGE与血管危险因素（如糖尿病、高血压、吸烟）之间的关联……
tldr: 该研究利用联邦学习在16个医疗中心1674名卒中患者的MRI数据上估计脑龄差（BrainAGE），在保护数据隐私的同时实现了接近集中式学习的预测性能，并揭示了BrainAGE与血管危险因素及卒中后功能结局的关联。
en_tdlr: This multicenter study shows that federated learning enables privacy-preserving BrainAGE estimation from MRI of 1674 stroke patients across 16 hospital centers, achieving performance comparable to centralized learning and revealing associations between BrainAGE and vascular risk factors as well as post-stroke functional outcomes.
